[mrdevil] My go-to almost daily since buying one about 6 months ago has been strawberry or mango yoghurt - just the generic tubs from Aldi (Mango) when available or from Coles / Woolies… fill the tuna, freeze them overnight, and you've got tasty healthy frozen yoghurt.
Fruit-wise, buy a can of slices pears, put them in with a little bit of juice to fill the gaps, freeze then blend… comes out incredibly creamy and tasty, like a pear icecream. I've been using pears as a base - adding other tinned fruits like mandarin slices, mango slices, raspberries, black cherries etc for some variety… all turns out excellent with very little work involved.
One must is to buy extra tubs though - I bought two additional sets of four generic tubs from Amazon, they work out about $10 each.

[jimmy c] Easy High-Protein Frozen Yoghurt
2 scoops Bulk Nutrients TMR or protein powder** — or 1 scoop of each
1 cup water**
About 1 cup full-fat Greek yoghurt** — a little less is fine, and even ½ a cup still works really well
½ teaspoon psyllium husk** as a thickener
½ a banana OR a handful to 1 cup of frozen berries**
Some people add a teaspoon of sugar, but I find the banana or fruit makes it sweet enough.
If you want to make it even healthier, you can throw in some frozen broccoli, spinach, carrots, etc. Try to match the vegetable to the flavour/colour if possible. The flavoured protein powder or Total Meal Replacement is strong enough to mask the "healthiness"!
I normally double all the ingredients and make two at a time .
If I think I'll want one before it has had a full 24 hours to freeze, I blend some ice into the cup of water and use frozen fruit and other cold ingredients. Starting with everything as cold as possible can knock a few hours off the freezing time.
[eggaz] frozen broccoli, spinach, carrots, etc.

[jimmy c] @eggaz: Same as I put in a smoothie sometimes. you cannot taste it if the protien powder flavour is strong enough.

[eggaz] I have the normal ninja creami, only just got it. I use one bottle.of the farmers union protein shake, put it on a soft ice cream cycle, clear the sides after first spin, add some mix ins (biscuit or other health-ish thing) and press the mix in button. Is a super easy low calorie ice cream.
My only complaint is how loud the machine is.
[dmac80] I love the Deluxe one, but on sale a couple of months ago. I don't really understand the 'prep is hard'' thing. It's as easy or difficult as you want. My go to is get one of those ready made protein drinks from Coles/Woolies, there's always one on brand on sale for half price, dump it in, add in 1/4 teaspoon xanthan gum, 2 tablespoons allulose, give it a mix, chuck it in the freezer and done for the week. You can get big batches of xanthan and allulose from Amazon. Xanthan gives it a creamier texture and allulose helps it taste sweet as freezing dulls the protein drink flavour a little. Protein ice cream at a fraction of the cost of the super markets.
